_required_contexts_note: A context belongs here only if it can actually FAIL. Eight were removed on
2026-08-03 because their sole substantive step carries `continue-on-error:
true`, so each job's only hard-failing steps are setup (checkout / uv /
maturin / netlist). They were required checks that could never block a
merge -- yet the aggregator still had to wait for every one of them to
COMPLETE, and completion is precisely what was timing out under queue
starvation. They accounted for ~45% of job-minutes and 8 of ~24 slots.
Removed: Extended Test Suites (bundle / workflow / checks), (cp-sat,
fast) and (cp-sat, slow x2); Invariant tests router_v6 groups 1, 2 and 4;
Invariant tests (io, deterministic, physics, fields, validation, cp_sat);
router_v6 group 3 is deliberately KEPT: it is the only invariant shard
whose test step is unmasked, i.e. the only one that is a real gate.
This is a capacity measure, not an absolution. The masks exist for
parallel-suite flakiness and carry TODOs to hard-fail after 2026-09-01.
The honest fix is pytest-rerunfailures, then REMOVING the masks and
returning these contexts to the required set -- not leaving them here
as decoration that costs runner slots and buys no safety.
_perf_ab_context_note: 2026-08-04 (Wave 4 Phase 0, R2): 'PR Performance Comparison' is a real
hard gate as of this date -- it exits non-zero on regression, fails closed
on a missing or empty baseline, and its continue-on-error mask is gone.
It was held OUT of required_contexts until the prerequisite below shipped;
the context_triggers section at the bottom of this file IS that
prerequisite, and the context was registered in #686 once it existed. The
paragraphs below are kept as the standing reason the two must stay
together: dropping context_triggers while leaving the context required
reintroduces the failure exactly.
Why: required_contexts_for_files returns EVERY context in this list as
soon as ANY of the ~90 trigger_paths match. Every context here today comes
from python-tests.yml, whose path list is drift-checked against this
manifest. pr-perf-check.yml is a DIFFERENT workflow with a narrower path
set. A PR touching only docs/plans/** or pcb/*.kicad_pro matches this
manifest but never fires pr-perf-check, so no check run is created --
'missing', not 'skipped', so verify_skips cannot rescue it. The aggregator
would poll timeout_seconds (2700) + backlog_grace_seconds (7200) = 2h45m
and then fail. That is a guaranteed red required check on every docs-only
PR, i.e. every open PR blocked at once.
Prerequisite (SHIPPED): a per-context workflow-trigger gate here (a
context_triggers section mapping a context to its own workflow's paths:
list), so a context can be dropped from the required set when its own
workflow legitimately does not fire.
Note that context_triggers mirrors pr-perf-check.yml's PULL_REQUEST paths.
That workflow also has a push trigger on main with the same path list, but
push runs create no PR check run, so only the pull_request list is what
this section has to track.
RESOLVED 2026-08-04 (same day): the committed baseline was CI-measured but
n=1 per benchmark, so the rolling median was that single row, nothing was
smoothed, and CI noise (<=9.9%) applied to it in full. The structural
cause was that pr-perf-check.yml triggered on `pull_request` ONLY, so no
row could ever be measured on main and the baseline could not grow. It now
also triggers on `push: branches: [main]` and workflow_dispatch, and in
that mode it captures instead of gating. The baseline is at n=6 per stage,
harvested from six CI runs of commits verified not to touch the
bottleneck-geometry module. Still do NOT re-capture locally: a
darwin-captured baseline measured -11% against linux CI on identical code,
which would blind the 20% margin to every regression below +35%.
Measurements and full reasoning:
docs/evidence/2026-08-04-perf-ab-harness-noise-floor.md
_fast_gates_note: 2026-08-05: 'Type Check', 'Generated Repo State' and 'LOC Cap Gate' were
three separate bare-runner jobs. They are now steps of the single 'Fast
Gates' job, together with the (never-required) known-failure pin registry
gate. No gate was dropped and no threshold moved -- the four gate commands
are byte-identical, they just share one runner slot and one `uv sync`
instead of building four Python environments for seconds of work.
Merging four slots into one is a capacity measure: measured across 33 PR
runs on 2026-08-05 those four jobs cost 4 of the ~12 slots a PR run of
python-tests.yml requests, and 10.4 of its 38.8 job-minutes, while the
actual gate commands take seconds. The dominant cost was four independent
uv environment builds (4m18s, 1m48s, 1m45s, 1m36s).
Coverage is unchanged; REPORTING GRANULARITY is not. A failure in any of
the four now reds one context instead of three distinct ones. Every gate
step carries `if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.setup.outcome == 'success' }}`,
so a red gate still lets the other three report their own verdict in the
same run -- the run log names which gate failed even though the context
does not. This is the same trade the 2026-07-28 gate split made in the
other direction, under the same idiom.
SEQUENCING (this file is read from base.sha, so ordering is load-bearing):
1. workflow-only PR adds the `fast-gates` job alongside the old four;
2. THIS manifest-only PR swaps the contexts -- it merges cleanly because
at merge time all five jobs still run and report;
3. workflow-only PR deletes the four now-unrequired jobs.
Collapsing 2 and 3 into one PR wedges that PR: its base manifest would
still demand contexts its own head no longer produces, so they report
'missing' forever and the aggregate times out.
_gate_vacuity_survey_note: PREREQUISITE FIX, same PR: scripts/check_required_checks.py's `_run` was
computing `required = manifest.required_contexts` unfiltered, so
`context_triggers` -- already shipped, already the documented fix for
the _perf_ab_context_note scenario below -- was never actually consulted
by the live polling loop; only its own pure-function unit tests exercised
it. Caught live: PR #1028 (docs-only) logged 'missing: PR Performance
Comparison' and failed. A second, opposite-direction bug shared the same
root cause: the early bail-out tested the GLOBAL trigger_paths list, so a
diff matching ONLY a context_triggers path absent from that global list
(e.g. firmware/** for the Firmware Tests addition below) would return
PASS without ever polling, even though that context's own workflow ran.
Both are fixed in `_run` itself now (see its own comment) -- required
context_triggers entries on real PRs are what the four additions below
were verified against, not merely the pure required_contexts_for_files
function. This is the reason it was safe to add four new cross-workflow
contexts in the same PR as this fix rather than after it: adding them
against the OLD `_run` would have wedged every PR matching the global
list but not each new context's own narrower paths (the (1) direction),
or silently never enforced them at all for the paths only each new
context's own workflow watches (the (2) direction, e.g. every
firmware-only PR).
2026-08-11/12 (docs/evidence/2026-08-11-gate-vacuity-audit.md finding 21):
the audit found FIVE workflows with hard-failing, unmasked steps that
trigger on pull_request against main but were absent from
required_contexts -- regression.yml, erc-gate.yml, golden-check.yml,
placer-regression.yml, firmware-tests.yml. golden-check.yml was
re-synced and its required_contexts wiring landed in #1032 (title claimed
the manifest was updated there; verified against the merged diff it was
not -- the workflow-side workflow_dispatch trigger and baseline fix
landed, this manifest entry is what actually finishes it).
The other four were surveyed here, individually, against live CI history
(gh run list --branch=main, most-recent 15 runs per workflow):
- erc-gate.yml (context 'ERC ratchet (kicad-cli sch erc)'): 2/2 runs
green on main (narrow trigger -- pcb/*.kicad_sch and its own
ceiling/script paths only). No continue-on-error. ADDED.
- placer-regression.yml (context 'Placer Regression (baseline-approval
gate)', renamed from the bare job id 'regression' in the same PR --
see the job's own comment): 13/15 success, 2/15 cancelled (PR
concurrency supersession, not failure) on the last 15 main runs. No
continue-on-error. ADDED.
- firmware-tests.yml (context 'Firmware Tests (state-machine +
fault-injection)', explicitly named in the same PR for the same
collision-avoidance reason): 15/15 success on the last 15 main runs.
No continue-on-error anywhere in the job -- R28/R29 exhaustive
reachability, invariant proofs, the R40 mutation sweep and SIL
fault-injection coverage are all hard gates today. ADDED.
- regression.yml (context 'regression' -- the live kicad-cli DRC-vs-
ceiling truth gate, and the only invocation of ci_check_drc.py in
the repo): NOT ADDED. Confirmed red on main at survey time -- 8
failure, 0 success, 7 cancelled across the last 15 main runs (`gh run
list --workflow=regression.yml --branch=main`), from two real
causes: test_golden_board_drc_regression failing, and
test_production_board_routing_drc_regression exiting 137 (OOM) on
the ubuntu-latest runner. Adding a currently-red workflow to
required_contexts wedges every PR immediately -- exactly the
failure mode #1032's own title warns against ('fix-then-require').
Follow-up, not applied here: fix the DRC regression and the OOM
(likely needs a larger runner or a lighter DRC sample count for this
job specifically), confirm green on main, THEN add 'regression' here
-- and note it collides by name with placer-regression.yml's job
unless that job's rename above is kept.
Each of the four additions got its own context_triggers entry below,
for the same reason 'PR Performance Comparison' has one (see
_perf_ab_context_note): each is owned by a workflow with a path filter
narrower than this manifest's global trigger_paths, so without an entry
here a PR that touches none of that workflow's own paths would still be
required to wait for a check-run GitHub never creates -- 'missing', not
'skipped', timing out the aggregate on every such PR.
